paper_title: 3D template-based $Fermi$-LAT constraints on the diffuse supernova axion-like particle background
suggested_experiment_name: Fermi-LAT DSNAL PB (Diffuse Supernova Axion-Like Particle Background)
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, canonical axion-photon coupling constant
notes: Template-based analysis of 12 years of Fermi-LAT data (50 MeV to 500 GeV) constraining the diffuse supernova axion-like particle background (DSNALPB). Main result: g_agamma ≲ 3.76×10^-11 GeV^-1 at 95% CL for m_a ≪ 10^-11 eV. This is a mass-independent bound valid over a wide range (encoded as horizontal line from 1e-11 to 1e4 eV). Systematic uncertainties from failed SN fraction, IMF, star formation rate, and GMF models yield a factor ~2 uncertainty, giving range [2.38, 7.04]×10^-11 GeV^-1. Improves upon Paper I (5.0×10^-11 GeV^-1) by including spatial morphology via template fitting and improved SN modeling. Slightly better than CAST bound but factor ~6 weaker than SN1987A gamma-ray burst limit. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.85, 31)) | Vision: Figure 10 shows 95% CL upper limits on g_agamma from Fermi-LAT observations of the diffuse gamma-ray background from core-collapse supernovae. The solid red line is the observed upper limit; the dashed line shows the DSNAL PB spectrum-only prediction. The exclusion region is ABOVE the red boundary. The plot includes 1σ and 2σ containment bands (green and yellow) from 250 Poisson realizations. Complementary constraints from SN 1987A γ-ray burst, Chandra (NGC 1275), and CAST (2017) are shown as colored regions. The analysis assumes the benchmark DSNAL PB scenario with varying fractions of failed core-collapse SNe. Mass range covers 1e-12 to 1e-7 eV; coupling range 1e-13 to 1e-9 GeV^-1.
